Legends & Prodigies, Round 6 - Live!
rubriker._rss_content: The second half of the "Legends & Prodigies" tournament in Madrid begins on Thursday morning with round six. After five rounds, David Antón leads with 4/5, half a point ahead of defending champion Faustino Oro. In round six, Oro has Black against Diego Flores, whom he defeated in the opening round, while Antón faces José Cuenca with White. The third game is José Martínez v Ivan Sokolov. | Live with commentary from 11:00 CEST. | Photo: Mar Melero

rubriker.title: Legends & Prodigies: David Antón scores twice to take sole lead
rubriker._rss_content: After six draws the previous day, the players at the Legends & Prodigies tournament in Madrid seemed ready for a fight: rounds four and five produced just one draw in six games. Faustino Oro beat Ivan Sokolov before drawing with Jose Eduardo Martinez Alcantara, while David Antón scored two wins, defeating Diego Flores and Sokolov. The experienced Spaniard now leads the young Argentine by half a point. | Photo: David Antón winning the 2025 Spanish Championship | Photo: Spanish Chess Federation

rubriker.title: Review: Opening Encyclopedia 2026
rubriker._rss_content: The ChessBase Opening Encyclopedia 2026 is one of the company’s flagship products alongside the Mega Database and the ChessBase database program - currently ChessBase'26. For years, these programs have formed part of the essential toolkit for everyday chess work. From the very beginning, the Opening Encyclopedia has played a key role by providing a fast and efficient overview of the entire spectrum of chess openings. Lukas Köpl took a closer look at the latest edition of the Opening Encyclopedia and summed up his impressions.

rubriker.title: Andrew Martin - The Evans Gambit is still dangerous
rubriker._rss_content: Andrew Martin presents the Evans Gambit as a dangerous and highly practical weapon for club players, especially those rated below 1800. Using a historic game by William Davies Evans, he shows how White gives up a pawn for rapid development, central control and direct attacking chances against the black king. Martin also explains why the opening remains relevant today despite modern engine analysis, with even top players such as Magnus Carlsen facing it in recent practice. The course is designed not only to teach a playable repertoire, but also to sharpen tactical vision and help players enjoy dynamic attacking chess.

rubriker.title: Mind vs Machine
rubriker._rss_content: 1997: Kasparov vs Deep Blue. We all know the story. But here is a new version told by three-time National Book Award finalist Steve Sheinkin, using first-hand accounts from grandmaster Maurice Ashley, with riveting illustrations by Eisner winner Thien Pham. The narrative, in comic book form, captures the excitement and suspense of a classic sports showdown and explores thought-provoking themes about where humanity stands at the rise of AI.

rubriker.title: El principio de parsimonia según Capablanca
rubriker._rss_content: El principio de parsimonia propone buscar la explicación más simple y eficiente sin sacrificar rigor. Aplicado al ajedrez, este criterio encuentra en José Raúl Capablanca una expresión ejemplar: claridad posicional, economía de medios y técnica precisa. El texto explora cómo su estilo refleja una forma de pensamiento que privilegia lo esencial sobre la complicación innecesaria. | Imagen (IA): Uvencio Blanco

rubriker.title: La chilena Damaris Abarca participará en histórica serie de torneos en la Antártida y el Polo Sur
rubriker._rss_content: La «Polar Chess Expedition» llevará el ajedrez hasta uno de los escenarios más extremos del planeta. Seis jugadores, representantes de los seis continentes habitados, disputarán un torneo válido para el rating FIDE en la Antártida y el polo sur geográfico. Encabezado por Nigel Short, el proyecto combina competición, aventura y vocación, con el propósito de certificar el torneo de ajedrez más austral de la historia.
